subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt the existing conflicting fork fix, ask for it to be refreshed in openclaw/openclaw, or clear that path and queue a narrow replacement fix?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the issue is currently paired with an open conflicting fork PR and a closed unmerged same-repo PR using the same patch idea, so automation should not create a duplicate branch until maintainers choose the contributor-path outcome.

options.title: Clear and replace with a narrow fix
options.body: Close or decline the stale conflicting branch path, then queue one focused gateway/TUI regression fix that uses the existing metadata stripper and display-name precedence.

options.title: Adopt the fork PR
options.body: Ask a maintainer or contributor to refresh the open fork PR against current main and review it as the canonical fix path.

options.title: Wait on contributor refresh
options.body: Keep the issue blocked on the existing fork PR, accepting that it remains conflicting and no target-repo fix is progressing.

recommendation.title: Clear and replace with a narrow fix
recommendation.body: Close or decline the stale conflicting branch path, then queue one focused gateway/TUI regression fix that uses the existing metadata stripper and display-name precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest routing owner from the original title-derivation merge plus repeated session/gateway history.
